ranked.headline: Ontology, network and causal priors are encoded directly into omics inference models
ranked.summary: Preprints and publications increasingly encode ontology, network, and causal priors within single-cell and multi-omics inference objectives.

ranked.headline: Structured prior knowledge integrated into learned models for drug and gene prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs graph, language, and knowledge-base representations with built-in attribution for drug, target, and gene prediction.

ranked.headline: Technical bias and annotation validity in scRNA-seq workflows
ranked.summary: Diagnostic tools now expose coverage bias, annotation errors and integration sensitivity before downstream single-cell interpretation.

ranked.headline: Computational tools resolve viral variants from epistatic, antigenic, and mixture data
ranked.summary: Epistatic coupling, antigenic cartography, and mixture quantification now provide variant-level readouts across SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and HIV-1.

ranked.headline: ML models link chromatin, sequence and expression data to gene regulatory programs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep learning and graph models to regulatory genomics data, including MPRA, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq.

ranked.headline: Interactive web platforms are linking genetic and molecular data to analysis workflows
ranked.summary: Harmonized data and knowledge graphs are being exposed through browser-accessible and pipeline-driven tools for reproducible reuse.

ranked.headline: Learned sequence models extend to enzyme, antibody, and genomic function prediction
ranked.summary: Protein and genomic language models are now paired with evolutionary priors, uncertainty estimates, and curated instruction datasets.

ranked.headline: Biology-based audits and mechanisms for neural and single-cell foundation models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether internal representations of neural and single-cell foundation models reflect biological mechanisms.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked computational methods for genomic variant, haplotype, and repeat analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply explicit ground-truth benchmarking to haplotype assembly, repeat genotyping, and structural variant analysis.

ranked.headline: Generative and graph models encode geometric constraints in antibody and peptide design
ranked.summary: Geometry-aware learned models now span antibody, cyclic peptide, membrane-active peptide, and lipid design across early 2026 preprints and publications.

ranked.headline: Graph-based and alignment tools advance strain-level and metagenomic sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report software for metagenomic profiling, plasmid reconstruction, pangenome alignment and viral sequence reduction.

ranked.headline: Generative and graph models infer spatial gene expression and tissue domains
ranked.summary: Recent work applies generative flow, graph, and transfer-learning models to spatial and single-cell omics prediction and annotation.

ranked.headline: Recombination and repeat expansion shape pathogen and parasitic plant genomes
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved and comparative genomes now resolve transposon, repeat and recombination dynamics across fungal pathogens and broomrape mitogenomes.

ranked.headline: Biophysical models predict how stiffness and fields steer cell engulfment and migration
ranked.summary: Recent models test how target stiffness, electric fields, and network geometry direct phagocytosis and immune cell navigation.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models infer selection and mutation from clonal and single-cell genomic data
ranked.summary: Sparse cross-sectional single-cell and clonal data now support Moran and diffusion models that infer selection and accumulation parameters.

ranked.headline: Single-cell multiomics link chromatin states to transcription across brain regions
ranked.summary: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and transcriptomic atlases now resolve regulatory programs in brain and basal ganglia at cell-type resolution.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and protein language models benchmarked against biological ground truth
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test LLM agents and protein language models against CRISPR screens, ProteinGym, and binding-affinity benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Generative models increasingly sample protein and RNA conformational states and dynamics
ranked.summary: Diffusion and latent-variable models now target microsecond trajectories and ligand dissociation pathways, not just static structures.

ranked.headline: Structured priors and spatial statistics sharpen pattern detection in omics data
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell omics methods now encode biological and spatial structure directly into representations and calibrated statistical tests.

ranked.headline: Multimodal and baseline-aware models advance genomic variant interpretation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers test learned variant-effect models against explicit baselines while integrating DNA, RNA, phenotype, and epigenomic evidence.

ranked.headline: Knowledge graphs map multi-target drug mechanisms and prioritize disease targets
ranked.summary: Knowledge graphs are now paired with explainable path identification, rule augmentation, and negative-sampling design for target discovery and repositioning.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic and learned models link drug response to tumor, imaging and omics data
ranked.summary: Quantitative models now integrate longitudinal imaging, single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to predict drug response and tumor dynamics.

ranked.headline: Learned embeddings are being refined and aligned across single-cell and omics data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply post-hoc refinement, group contrastive losses, and meta-learning to biological embeddings across multiple data modalities.

ranked.headline: Learned representations segment tissue and nuclei in gigapixel and whole-organ images
ranked.summary: Pretrained foundation models and self-supervised pretraining are now applied directly to gigapixel pathology and whole-organ tomography data.

ranked.headline: Pretraining objectives and encodings reshape DNA, protein and molecular language models
ranked.summary: Scaling, representation, and evolutionary pretraining questions are now being tested directly in molecular, protein, and genome language models.

ranked.headline: Tools extract dynamic, ligand, and metal-binding features from protein structures
ranked.summary: Several new Python and ML tools released in early 2026 target dynamic interfaces, pKa shifts, docking, and metal-site prediction in protein structures.

ranked.headline: Structured heterogeneity yields analytic outcome criteria in epidemic and microbial models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published dispersal model encode heterogeneity directly into reduced analytic objects that predict outcomes.

ranked.headline: Transcriptomic tools extend analysis to flux, communication, and spatial layers
ranked.summary: Recent publications apply transcriptomic integration to metabolic modeling, multi-omics modules, and single-cell spatial analysis at scale.

ranked.headline: Tools standardize force field parameters, vesicle data, plots and omics metadata
ranked.summary: Browser-based and agent-driven access now wraps curated parameters, vesicle measurements and plot generation in standardized, shareable workflows.

ranked.headline: Reannotation finds ~4000 bifunctional human genes; plant proteostasis modules mapped
ranked.summary: Gene and protein annotations are being re-evaluated against existing evidence, from bifunctional gene catalogues to noncanonical protein degradation features.

ranked.headline: Nanopore and GPU pipelines cut compute for telomere-to-telomere and population genomics
ranked.summary: Reducing genome processing costs from $100 to under $1 makes recomputable pangenomics practical at population scale.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks of ML models for variant filtering, methylation, and binding site prediction
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks test whether complex deep models outperform simpler baselines across genomic tasks, including pediatric T-ALL outcome prediction.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved assembly extends to autopolyploid potato and phased apple genomes
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved assemblies now reach autopolyploid potato and phased apple cultivar genomes, with near telomere-to-telomere contiguity reported for potato.

ranked.headline: Bias-corrected RNA-seq methods recover transcript-level quantities from count data
ranked.summary: Spike-in, normalization, and polyadenylation and circRNA detection studies now address measurement bias in RNA-seq quantification.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and interpretable models advance computational toxicity prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers test toxicity and activity models against cross-species clinical data and standardized peptide benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Simulations link conformational ensembles and interface residues to coupling and gating
ranked.summary: Simulation-derived free energies and ensembles now resolve how single residues and monomer conformations shape protein interaction outcomes.

ranked.headline: Orthology-aware web and cloud tools scale comparative omics and phylogenomic analyses
ranked.summary: Recent items present scalable, web-accessible and cloud platforms for orthology, phylogenomic and functional analysis across species.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking LC-MS acquisition and search tools for proteome depth and quantification
ranked.summary: Shorter DIA gradients and multi-platform acquisition raise demands on search engines, QC monitoring, and cross-platform benchmarking in proteomics.

ranked.headline: Computational methods infer tumor DNA features and microbial contamination from sequencing
ranked.summary: Long-read, single-cell and cfDNA methylome data now allow computational separation of genuine biological features from technical confounders.

ranked.headline: Computational tools link microbial genomes and metabolites to xenobiotic transformations
ranked.summary: Preprints from early 2026 pair curated microbial metabolite knowledge with long-read genome mining and time-resolved molecular networking.
